claim: The transactional outbox exists and 'nothing happens without an emission' is a checked property rather than a slogan. Emission lives inside CanonJournal's landing path, so no code path can land a record without emitting: append, supersede and revoke each emit exactly once; a write rejected by validation emits nothing; an idempotent re-land of identical content emits nothing new. Event ids are gapless and monotonic from zero, the event stream and the hash-linked receipt chain agree change-for-change, and replay from EVERY cursor position -- including the null backfill cursor and every mid-stream reconnect point -- reconstructs the full stream with nothing missing, which is P10's stated 'no event loss' criterion. A cursor ahead of the stream returns silence rather than throwing. Events name a revision and carry minimumAccess so fan-out can decide who may be told without reading content back; a vector confirms no record content appears in an event. The integrity checker is proven able to fail on all four of its finding classes. Over the real 226-record corpus every landed record announced exactly once. 10/10 vectors; 163/163 across fifteen packages.

claim: R2 has delivery. A new subscriber receives a backfill burst of everything it may see, live delivery follows, and replay from EVERY cursor position -- the null backfill cursor and every mid-stream reconnect point -- loses nothing the subscriber may see, which is P10's stated no-event-loss criterion. A subscriber beyond the burst limit receives an explicit lagged disclosure naming catch-up-then-live, and catchUp() executes that recovery to a terminating non-lagged phase. Lag is measured in the subscriber's own relevant stream, not the global one: a vector makes 100 changes to a subject the subscriber cannot see and asserts the delivery is NOT lagged, because reporting the global figure would turn the lag message into a side channel for write volume. A lens narrows only -- a lens naming a subject outside the accessible dependency set grants nothing. Silence stays silence: a caught-up subscriber and a subscriber whose invisible neighbour changed both receive no message rather than an empty one. The wire carries invalidation keys and never content. 10/10 vectors; 209 across seventeen packages.

details.patternAcrossFindings: All three defects share a shape this project keeps producing: a guarantee stated in prose beside code that provides it only partially. The equivalence checker's comment described a leak scan, and the scan compared spellings. NR-scms-005 said promotion refuses unauthorised candidates while nothing checked authority. The prose is not decoration -- it is where the intent is recorded -- but it is not enforcement, and the gap between them is where these defects live.

claim: SH-14 is closed by deciding it rather than by patching around it. Observations are signals about subjects, not participants in a surface, so freeze() still never turns one into a subject -- but it now projects them into a separate `observations` collection, and observationsFor(snapshot, subject, access) reads them. The separation from `subjects` is what makes 'an observation is not a participant' structural: nothing that reads members can reach these. Access is the observation's own rather than its subject's, so a private note about a public article stays private, verified by a vector. SCMS-028's derived Semantic Article Field, which had been landing in Canon and becoming invisible to everything including its owner, is now reachable. 16/16 canon vectors; 224 across eighteen packages.

claim: The composed proof matches the landed surface again. Since SCMS-027 last reconciled it, the system gained emission (032), the wire (033/034), derived freshness (035), the editor as a surface (044/047) and the site as a third adapter (037) -- each vectored alone, none shown composing. Four new seams close that: every governed write in the composed run emitted with receipt/event parity and gapless ids; the wire delivers the run's changes to a subscriber with visible dependencies and never the hidden subject, while a subscriber with an empty dependency set gets silence rather than an empty message; freshness in the composed world cannot claim liveness before a delivery and reads 'live, checked 4s ago' only after a real one; and the editor and the site resolve as two expressions of the same Canon, neither showing the hidden subject, with the editor seeing surface vocabulary and the page seeing container forms. The composite invariant gains a third extension. 18/18 e2e vectors; 232 across eighteen packages.

claim: The E8 arc closes end to end. The editor gained qualify and promote routes, and the site replays the owner's governed actions through the same contract registry, so a promotion made in the editor is visible to a reader. Verified by driving the real servers against the real corpus: qualify produced a QUALIFIED attestation, promote moved publicationState to promoted, the site replayed 4 actions with 2 promoted, and /writing rendered 1 card with 1 matching RSS item -- while a promoted PRIVATE article produced zero cards, because promotion decides publication and access still decides audience.

details.replayDesign: Replay goes THROUGH the contracts rather than restoring serialized state, so a replayed action crosses exactly the gates the original crossed and a log entry cannot smuggle in something the contracts would refuse. Refusals -- expired evidence, for instance -- are counted and reported at startup rather than swallowed, and the record simply is not published.
details.disclosureAtPointOfUse: The qualify route writes independentEvaluator:false on every evidence record, truthfully, and returns a disclosure stating that the owner attested to their own work and that nothing currently requires an independent evaluator (SH-13). Building a workflow through a known-weak gate is defensible only if the weakness is visible where someone meets it.

details.notEstablished: Development-grade custody, NOT the durability decision (SH-1). A local file outside the repository, no shared database, no concurrency control between the two processes, and the site rebuilds at startup rather than following changes live.

claim: replayActions is vectored, raising it from interaction-only evidence to the rung the rest of the system sits at. claim: SH-20 is closed as a DECLARED NON-PROPERTY rather than by adding enforcement. checkEquivalence now reports intraGroupOrderMatched without making it a pass criterion, and a vector asserts both halves: reversing a group's members in one expression still passes S3, and the report says the order did not hold. Priority is semantic and its realization is free, so an adapter may order a group by reading time, alphabet, or nothing at all -- the absence of the guarantee is correct. What was wrong is that it was true by omission, and an unwritten missing guarantee is indistinguishable from one people assume they have.

claim: Supersession and revocation are derived rather than stored, so no code path rewrites a landed row. The successor carries the supersedes pointer and a revoke receipt carries revocation, both of which are append-only by construction. Rows live in a private array nothing assigns into; JournalEntry keeps its public shape, projected at read time. Four vectors: superseding rewrites no row (every pre-existing envelope byte-identical after); revoking rewrites no row; the derived indexes are only a cache, proven by recomputing from rows and receipts alone and comparing against what the journal uses; and current() is expressible as the query it will become in Postgres -- a row is current when nothing supersedes it and no revoke receipt names it -- computed in the vector without the journal's indexes. 20/20 canon vectors, full suite green.

claim: Canon has a Postgres schema in which append-only is enforced by grant rather than by code. canon_record keys on the content hash; canon_receipt carries the chain by prev_hash rather than seq contiguity; canon_outbox is written only by a SECURITY DEFINER trigger on receipt insert, so an event exists if and only if a receipt does, and the trigger pg_notifys on the native channel section 8.1 requires. canon_current and canon_revoked are views, expressing SCMS-056's derivation where it belongs. A unique partial index on supersedes makes a second successor impossible so current cannot fork. The conformance suite is fifteen checks run against a real database: as the runtime role, UPDATE and DELETE on records and receipts, a forged outbox row and DELETE on the outbox all fail; the controls confirm the runtime can append, that appending emits, and that receipt/event parity holds.

claim: Content-addressed storage for prose and media exists, closing SH-4, which proposed the model and which nothing had adopted. canon_blob keys on the sha256 digest, so identical bytes stored twice are refused by the primary key and deduplication is a consequence of naming rather than a background job. The identity was already in the model: the corpus manifest has carried bodySha256 for every entry since SCMS-028, so this is the store that digest was pointing at. A CHECK constraint requires byte_length to equal length(bytes), so the manifest and the store cannot drift apart silently. Blobs are immutable by grant -- a blob is bytes named by their own hash, and changing the bytes under the name would make the name a lie -- so the runtime role may INSERT and SELECT and nothing else. Unreferenced blobs are identifiable through a view rather than deletable, since deletion is not available to the runtime at all. Six new refusal checks, 21 in total.

claim: A page materializes as a static artifact: bytes named by their own content digest, carrying the surface fingerprint as a separate invalidation key. Seven vectors over the owner's real corpus. Materializing is deterministic -- same Canon, same bytes, same digest -- which is what makes Cache-Control: immutable honest rather than optimistic. Access is part of the artifact key, so a cache handed artifacts cannot serve one across levels by accident. A public artifact carries no private subject in its bytes or its dependency set, and a change to a private subject does not invalidate it, because the dependency set was computed after access projection and a change a reader cannot observe cannot appear in it. Two adapters of one surface share a fingerprint and differ in digest, so they invalidate together and are addressed separately.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested. The module is pure: it computes what to store and writes nothing. Nothing is served from an artifact yet, and nothing persists one -- storage is SCMS-065 and serving is unbuilt.

details.twoKeysNotOne: digest and fingerprint are deliberately separate. Two surfaces with different dependency sets can render byte-identical output -- an empty index and a filtered one, say -- and must still invalidate independently. Keying only by content would silently merge them and one would go stale.
details.designNote: The fingerprint is the only sound name for a static page because SSS 26 computes it over the ACCESSIBLE dependency set, so it is access-safe by construction rather than by a check. This is the same rule canon_blob already follows for prose and media.

claim: Full document review and audit. Mechanical sweep across every document and record found NO dangling references -- 22 SH entries, 67 work items, 18 negative results, 58 evidence records and 3 blockers all resolve, and every work file has a graph row. Eight findings recorded in research/audit-2026-08-29.md. Four were register drift and are fixed: the composed-proof claim was stale by ten vectors (8 cited, 18 actual); the expression claim understated the system at two adapters when there are three, and omitted that its own conformance checker was corrected twice in two days; a blocker read 'P7/P22' after P22 was accepted, which is the same staleness I had fixed in the graph hours earlier without checking whether the sentence appeared elsewhere; and 'declared content types are enforced' was materially overstated, being true of the contract runtime and false of the system, since governedImport never supplied the validator. Three capabilities -- the Postgres store, blobs, materialization -- had evidence and no claim row, now added.

claim: An edit in the editor reaches a reader's open page. An SSE endpoint pushes invalidation keys per section 8.3 -- keys, never content -- and the client re-fetches through the same route it first rendered, so the channel cannot become a second read path with its own access rules. Driven end to end against the real corpus: promote in the editor, the site replays the increment through the contracts, deliver filters per subscriber, and the public client receives exactly one key ('active-object-callouts', phase live) with zero evidence or attestation ids. A connecting client receives only 'ready' with the position it is caught up to, and no spurious wave. Six vectors cover the non-leak, silence, keys-not-content, and the refused-action case.

PROJECT_TYPE and ROLE_TYPE are derived from what the corpus actually carries: roles always have company, period and skills; projects always have category. ContentTypeSchema gained attr declarations, and checkArticle was generalized to checkContent over any kind. The four call sites that each carried `contentKind === article || note ? check : NOT_APPLICABLE` now ask a single typeFor() registry -- four chances to disagree collapsed to one.

details.designDecision: Slots are CLOSED and attrs are OPEN, deliberately. Slots are the authored structure the type owns, so an undeclared slot is a finding. Attrs are metadata carried from the source, and the corpus demonstrably has one-off attrs on single entries -- one note carries `awards`, another `stats` -- so closing the set would make the type reject real content rather than describe it. That is NR-scms-016's lesson pointed the other way.
details.requiredVsMerelyPresent: Required attrs are the ones definitional for the kind, not the ones the import happens to always carry. `featured` and `force` are present on all nine projects and are presentational; requiring them would encode the Medium import's shape as the type's law and make a hand-created project invalid. A role without an employer, a period or skills is not an under-described role -- it is a different thing -- so those three are required.
details.vectorCaughtAnOmission: The vector asking every type the same question -- does it require `listed`? -- failed on ARTICLE_TYPE, which I had given the attr to three types and not the fourth. `listed` is load-bearing because the reader's discovery lens includes on it, so an absent value must fail rather than default (NR-scms-004). It is now declared once and shared, so a new type cannot quietly omit it.
details.fixturesNotWeakened: Adding the requirement failed six pre-existing fixtures across schema, qualification and e2e that predate the attr. The fixtures were given `listed: true` -- which every real record carries -- rather than the type being relaxed to accommodate them.

claim: The claim register is now checked against the work graph. scripts/check-claim-register.py asserts four things: every SCMS-NNN the register cites exists in the graph; a claim at an Implemented or Tested rung cites at least one Done item, so a claim resting entirely on Ready or Blocked work is caught as a claim about intentions; a claim citing Blocked work is itself hedged; and a claim naming a proposal as blocking it does not name one DESIGN.md records as accepted. Self-test proves all four detections fire. The real register passes at 27 claims.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested. Checks agreement between two registers; makes no judgement about whether cited evidence SUPPORTS a claim, which is what the adversarial passes are for and which a gate pretending to do it would do worse than not at all.
details.theRuleThatMattered: The first three rules did not catch the finding the gate was built for. The stale row read 'blocked on P7/P22', cited a Done item, and hedged nothing -- so all three passed it. The staleness lived in prose about PROPOSALS, not in a citation to blocked work. Rather than soften the claim, rule 4 was added: proposal dispositions are read from DESIGN.md's own [PNN - accepted] markers and a row naming an accepted proposal as blocking is reported.
details.falsePositiveCaught: Rule 4's first run fired on the very row the audit had already corrected -- 'blocked on P7 only (P22 was accepted 2026-08-28...)' -- reading the parenthetical that RECORDS the fix as though it were the defect. The blocking clause is now bounded at the first parenthesis, semicolon or em dash, because what follows those is explanation rather than claim. SCMS-069's own Ready predicate names this as a stop condition: a gate that cries wolf on honest rows is one people learn to ignore.
details.processNote: The gate was tested against the actual historical row before being trusted, which is how both the gap and the false positive were found. Asserting that a new gate would have caught a past finding is cheap; running it against that finding is not.

claim: A Done work item must now carry a work file or a stated exemption. check-work-graph.py gained a fourth rule and a self-test proving it fires, and the thirteen Done items that lack a Ready predicate carry a marker saying so -- eleven recording that the discipline lapsed on 2026-08-29 with a pointer to the audit, and two recording that they were delivered inside another item and never separately scoped.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested. Enforces that a predicate exists or its absence is stated; makes no judgement about a predicate's quality, which is unmeasurable.
details.theFixNotBeingWorseThanTheGap: The obvious response to thirteen items without predicates is to write thirteen predicates. That would be worse than the gap. A Ready predicate is valuable BECAUSE it was written before the work, when it could still constrain what got built; composed afterwards from what happened, it produces a document that looks like governance and functions as decoration -- and this project has enough declarations that nothing consumes. A truthful marker is honest in a way an invented predicate is not.

claim: Embargoes exist. A promoted record carrying attrs.embargoUntil is ineligible for a reader until the resolution's declared temporal coordinate reaches that instant, and visible to the owner throughout. Five vectors: absent before the instant, present at and after it, an absent coordinate failing closed, the owner unaffected, and the same snapshot resolving two different ways at two coordinates with the earlier coordinate replaying to a byte-identical fingerprint.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested at the resolver. Nothing sets an embargo yet -- promote takes no embargo input -- so this is the reading half. The writing half is a contract change and is not claimed.
details.noWallClock: Nothing in the resolver reads the time, asserted by grepping impl/surface-resolver for Date.now and new Date. A record becomes readable because a LATER RESOLUTION IS ASKED at a later coordinate, not because something woke up. That keeps embargo replayable -- re-asking an earlier coordinate reproduces the earlier surface, fingerprint included -- and needs no scheduler, no background job, and no cache invalidation at the instant.
details.absentIsNotNow: A caller declaring no coordinate sees embargoed content as ineligible rather than the resolver assuming the current time. Guessing the other way publishes early, which section 6 treats as the unrecoverable direction. This is NR-scms-004's rule -- spell it so a missing value fails closed -- applied to time rather than to a flag.
details.ineligibleNotWithheld: Before its instant the record is not a gated participant, it is simply not yet part of the readable world, exactly like an unpromoted draft. Withheld would have disclosed that something exists and is coming, which is a different claim and one the author did not make.
details.placedPerTheLifecycle: A first draft applied the embargo during PROJECT ACCESS, which is wrong: SSS section 31 orders PROJECT ACCESS before BIND CONTEXT, so the coordinate is not yet bound there. It belongs in EVALUATE ELIGIBILITY, as a peer of the entitlement gate.

claim: Evidence tone exists -- the half of SPS's morphologyFor that SCMS-008 sent to neither SSS nor the expression recipe. evidenceTone reads a group's membership and returns earned, steady, fading, or unevidenced, with the counts and a basis string a person can check against the records. details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested as a pure function. It is not yet surfaced in the editor's panel, so nothing displays it -- the reading exists and no reader consumes it, which is stated here rather than implied away.
details.boundaryHeld: Tone is semantic, so it may say `fading` and may not say smaller, greyer, later or spoken last. SSS-INV-008 forbids semantic priority prescribing graphical presentation and SSS-INV-009 puts morphology outside SSS; a vector asserts the reading mentions none of hero, rail, grid, matrix, card, large, small, top, first, centered, bleed or column.
details.whyNotInTheResolver: freeze() carries publicationState into a snapshot and not evidenceState, so the resolver cannot see evidence and should not -- it resolves from a frozen snapshot while evidence lives in Canon. Tone is therefore computed OVER a resolved membership rather than during resolution.
details.distinctionKept: Evidence that lapsed (STALE, SUPERSEDED) is counted separately from evidence that never existed, and lapsed evidence dominates the reading: a grouping mostly held up by expired checks is fading whatever its raw count, because the count is the thing that has stopped being true. That is section 6's unrun-versus-failed distinction applied to time.
details.knownGap: The tone is not yet shown anywhere. SCMS-072's predicate calls for exposing it on the SCMS-047 surface panel, and that half is not done.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested. The reading now has a consumer, which is what was missing when this was recorded Partly done.

claim: SCMS-073 is closed. content.promote@1 accepts an optional embargoUntil instant, so an embargo can now be set rather than only honoured. Promotion still happens immediately -- the publication axis moves, the receipt is written, the outbox emits -- and only readability is deferred, which is why no scheduler is needed. A malformed instant is refused as invalid_input rather than ignored, because ignoring it would read as 'no embargo' downstream and publish early. Absent input leaves no attribute behind. Driven end to end: promoted with embargoUntil 2027-01-01, a public reader at 2026-09-01 resolves nothing and at 2027-06-01 resolves the record.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested, both halves. The reading half landed in scms-evidence-073; this is the writing half that made it usable.
details.failClosed: Four malformed instants were tried -- 'soon', an impossible date, a Unix epoch integer, and the empty string -- and each is refused with nothing promoted. Accepting any of them would have published immediately.

claim: The Postgres schema has a reader. impl/store/src/adapter.ts writes a record and its receipt in one transaction -- so the outbox trigger fires inside the same commit, which is section 8.1's requirement made structural rather than remembered -- and reads records back with supersession and revocation derived by the views. Five conformance vectors against a real Postgres 17. The load-bearing one: a corpus written through the adapter, read back, and resolved produces a surface with the SAME FINGERPRINT as one resolved from the in-memory journal, so every resolver, expression and reader vector already written applies to the durable store rather than needing to be rewritten against it.

details.claimLadder: Implemented + Tested against real Postgres. Establishes round-trip fidelity and that the grants bind the adapter like anything else. Establishes NOTHING about connection pooling, retries, concurrent writers, migration ordering, or production operation -- and nothing in impl/ has been switched over to it yet, which is deliberate: the adapter earns trust by agreeing with the journal before anything depends on it.
details.firstRuntimeDependency: pg 8.13.1, pinned exactly, this project's first. Zero dependencies was never doctrine -- it appears in no canonical document -- and section 12.1 says to consume capabilities as pinned dependencies rather than reinvent them, which implementing the Postgres wire protocol would be. The lockfile is committed and CI runs npm ci.
details.whatItDoesNotDo: It does not replace CanonJournal. The journal is the semantics, vectored across twenty packages; the adapter makes those semantics durable. That is why the vectors compare the two rather than testing the adapter alone.
details.receiptSuppliedNotComputed: landRecord takes the receipt rather than computing it, because the hash chain is Canon's and computing it in the store would put the chain in two places -- and the chain's whole value is that there is one.
details.testIsolationCorrected: Two vectors initially failed by comparing global counts against a per-test journal while the database accumulated across tests. Scoped to each test's own subjects, which is also the more honest shape: a real store is shared.

claim: The ten formal-resource pins are now falsifiable. scripts/verify-pins.py fixes one digest procedure (fpb-aggregate-v1), verifies git-revision pins by commit existence, digest pins by recomputation, and declared inventories by presence. Before: OK=2, UNREPRODUCIBLE=7, REMOTE=1, and no code anywhere read the field. After restamping: OK=9, REMOTE=1.

details.claimLadder: Demonstrated, and bounded. The verifier establishes that nine mounts match what the manifest records TODAY, and that two git revisions exist. It does NOT establish that the recorded digests describe what was pinned on 2026-08-28 -- for the seven restamped pins that state is unrecoverable, because the original procedure was never written down. priorDigest preserves the old values as evidence that they never held.
details.procedure: fpb-aggregate-v1: walk the mount excluding .git/node_modules/.DS_Store and symlinks; sha256 each file; sort by mount-relative POSIX path in byte order; digest = sha256 of 'path:filehash' lines joined by newline, no trailing newline. Step 4 is the aggregate FPB's own gen-context.py computes, so the project holds one digest idea rather than two.
details.beforeState: 48 candidate procedures were tried against the fpb pin -- chosen because its source is an immutable released package, so drift could not explain a mismatch -- across four exclusion sets, dotfile and .DS_Store variants, and three aggregation forms. None reproduced the recorded digest. revisionOrDigest appeared in four places across both trees and no script read it.
details.verifiedNotAssumed: Two things I expected to be findings were not. sss ships EMPTY schemas/ and conformance/ directories, which the manifest already records in caps as UD-13. All nine local mounts hold every path in their declared inventory, zero missing, including icp which is a legitimate three-file protocol. Both were checked before being described.

Against the real manifest, zeroing the sss digest produces DRIFT and exit 1; restoring returns exit 0.

Six mounts are directories not under version control, so a digest detects drift without preventing it or saying what drifted.
